[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Shared VPC host-project operation uses the Compute Engine Shared VPC feature, but has no ordering dependency on API activation. Ensure configured project services complete before enabling the host role, so the Compute API is available first.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Shared VPC host-project operation uses the Compute API, but it has no ordering edge to the project service activations. If compute.googleapis.com is enabled by this module, wait for project_services before configuring the host project to avoid an API-not-enabled failure.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host enables the Shared VPC feature, which is a Compute Engine capability and requires compute.googleapis.com to be enabled on the project first. project_services enables the requested APIs but nothing orders shared_vpc_host after it, so the host-enablement can run before the Compute API is active and fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host enables Shared VPC on local.project.project_id, which requires the Compute Engine API (compute.googleapis.com) to already be enabled on that project. That API is enabled by google_project_service.project_services when it is listed in var.services, but there is no attribute reference or depends_on connecting them, so the host-project resource can race ahead of API activation and fail.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host` enables the Shared VPC host feature on this project, an operation that requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the project. It has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`, so it may run before (or concurrently with) service activation and fail on a fresh apply. Its sibling resource `google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.service_projects` already depends on the host resource; the host resource itself should be ordered after the enabled services.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host` enables the Shared VPC host feature via the Compute Engine (XPN) API, which requires the Compute API to be enabled in this project. Nothing in the resource's configuration references `google_project_service.project_services`, so on a brand-new project Terraform may attempt to enable the host feature before the APIs are active and fail.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Associating this project as a Shared VPC service project requires the Compute Engine Shared VPC API, but this resource has no dependency on configured API activation. Order it after project services to avoid attempting the association before the Compute API is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
Assigning this project as a Shared VPC service project uses the Compute API, but this resource has no ordering edge to the service activations for the current project. If compute.googleapis.com is enabled by this module, wait for project_services before creating the association.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, relying on compute.googleapis.com being enabled on the project. It references the project only through local.project.project_id (string) and does not depend on google_project_service.project_services, so the attachment can be attempted before the Compute API is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches local.project.project_id as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute Engine API (compute.googleapis.com) to be enabled on the service project. google_project_service.project_services enables that API, but nothing orders the attachment after API activation, so it can fail.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute Engine API to already be enabled in the service project. It currently has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`, so on a fresh apply the attachment can race against (and fail ahead of) API enablement. Every other API-consuming resource in this module (e.g. `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`) explicitly depends on the enabled services; this resource should too.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project via a Compute Engine (XPN) API call, which fails on a newly created project unless the Compute API (and other services in `var.services`) are already enabled. No attribute reference or depends_on expresses ordering against `google_project_service.project_services`, so Terraform may apply the attachment before API activation completes.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots grants host-project roles to this project's robot service accounts (e.g. service-<num>@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com), which only exist once the corresponding APIs are enabled by google_project_service.project_services. The members are computed strings via local.service_accounts_robots, so no attribute reference orders the binding after service enablement; without it, granting to not-yet-created service accounts can fail.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles to robot service accounts from `local.service_accounts_robots`, but those robots (`service-<num>@compute-system...`, etc.) are only created once their APIs are enabled by `google_project_service.project_services`. There is no dependency on `project_services` (the parallel `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek`, which uses the same robot accounts, explicitly depends on it), so the IAM grant can run before the principals exist and fail.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles on the host project to this project's service-agent robot accounts (e.g. `service-NUMBER@gcp-sa-*`), constructed from `local.service_accounts_robots` / `local.service_account_cloud_services`. Those robot service identities only come into existence once the corresponding APIs are enabled in this project — exactly the ordering that the parallel resource `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` enforces via its explicit `depends_on` on `google_project_service.project_services`. `shared_vpc_host_robots` has no such dependency, so the grants may be created before the identities they target exist.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` grants roles in the host project to this project's service robot identities (e.g. `service-<num>@gcp-sa-*`, `service_account_cloud_services`). These robot service accounts are only created when their corresponding APIs are enabled in this project, but the resource has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`, so the IAM grant can race API activation and fail with a nonexistent-serviceAccount error.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots grants roles in the host project to this project's Google-managed robot service identities (e.g. service-NUMBER@gcp-sa-*). These service accounts are only created after the corresponding APIs are enabled, i.e. after google_project_service.project_services completes (SA creation is asynchronous following API activation). Without this dependency Terraform may attempt the IAM grant before the robot service account exists and the API will reject the unknown member. The module already expresses this ordering for every other consumer of these identities (see google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek and the service_accounts output), but this resource has none.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
For the just-in-time services (`secretmanager`, `pubsub`, `cloudasset`), the robot service account referenced by `google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots` is only created when `google_project_service_identity.jit_si` runs (it does not appear merely from API activation). If `shared_vpc_service_config.service_identity_iam` targets one of these services, the IAM grant can be applied before the service identity exists; `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_identity_cmek` handles this with an explicit `depends_on` on `jit_si`, and `shared_vpc_host_robots` should as well.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
When service_identity_iam is configured for a just-in-time service (secretmanager, pubsub, cloudasset), the referenced member is the service identity that google_project_service_identity.jit_si explicitly triggers into existence; that generation is an asynchronous operation (create timeout of 20 minutes) and the service account does not exist until it succeeds. google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots references these identities but has no dependency on jit_si, so the IAM grant can race ahead of identity creation and fail with an unknown member error.
